{{short description|British statistician and epidemiologist}}
'''Nicholas Edward Day''', [[CBE]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 24 September 1939)<ref name=debretts/> is a retired [[statistician]] and [[cancer epidemiology|cancer epidemiologist]].<ref name=debretts>{{cite web|title=Prof Nicholas Day, CBE, FRS|url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/d/15365/Nicholas%20Edward+DAY.aspx|work=[[Debrett's People of Today]]|accessdate=12 June 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323205553/http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/d/15365/Nicholas%20Edward+DAY.aspx|archive-date=23 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==

He was educated at [[Gresham's School]] and the [[University of Oxford]], from 1958-1962, where he gained a B.A. in Mathematics and a Diploma in Statistics, and the [[University of Aberdeen]] from 1962-1966, where he obtained a Doctorate of Philosophy.{{cn|date=November 2018}}

==Career==
Day worked at the [[International Agency for Research on Cancer]] in [[Lyon]] from 1969 to 1986, where he rose to become head of the Unit of [[Biostatistics]] and [[Field study|Field Studies]].<ref name=debretts/>
He was director of the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] Biostatistics Unit from 1986 to 1989, and continued as honorary director until 1999.<ref name=debretts/> From 1997 until his retirement in 2004 he was co-director of the [[Strangeways Research Laboratory]] in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=Directors of Strangeways Research Laboratory|url=http://www.srl.cam.ac.uk/directors.html|publisher=Strangeways Research Laboratory|accessdate=12 June 2010|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303202518/http://www.srl.cam.ac.uk/directors.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also professor of [[public health]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] from 1989 to 1999, and professor of [[epidemiology]] from 1999 until 2004.<ref name=debretts/>

Day was made a [[CBE|Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] in the [[2001 New Year Honours]] for services to statistics and epidemiology underpinning cancer biology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/in_depth/uk/2000/new_year_honours_2000/1092605.stm| publisher=[[BBC News]]| title=New Years Honours 2000: DBEs to CBEs|accessdate=12 June 2010|date=30 December 2000}}</ref>

His hobbies include [[sea angling|sea fishing]] and tree growing.<ref name=debretts/>

==Books==
* 1980 (with [[Norman Breslow]]), ''Statistical Methods in Cancer Research: Volume 1—The Analysis of [[case-control study|Case-Control Studies]]''. [[International Agency for Research on Cancer]], Lyon, France. {{ISBN|978-92-832-0182-3}}.
* 1986 (with Matti Hakama & Anthony B. Miller) ''Screening for cancer of the uterine cervix''. International Agency for Research on Cancer, Lyon, France. {{ISBN|978-92-832-1176-1}}
* 1987 (with Norman Breslow), ''Statistical Methods in Cancer Research: Volume 2—The Design and Analysis of [[Cohort study|Cohort Studies]]''. International Agency for Research on Cancer, Lyon, France. {{ISBN|978-92-832-1182-2}}.
* 1988 (edited with Anthony B. Miller) ''Screening for Breast Cancer''. Huber. {{ISBN|978-0-920887-26-4}}.
